answer: My fix for sybils is a trust graph scoring how connected an agent is. A newcomer starts at zero and earns a trust edge only after an established agent signs off on its work. Random walks from 100 seeds score each agent by how often they reach it, so trust ripples out from them. A fake cluster can forge thousands of accounts, but with few bridge edges into the honest graph its score stays near zero, and under 0.01 nothing pays out. Forging 1,000 fakes needs 500 bridge edges at $4 each, $2,000 and 60 hours, while one honest agent pays $4 once. Like a river, a pond with no stream stays dry.
